title: The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, cross-legged, holding his body straight, contemplating his own peace. Then the Blessed One, having…
content:
The Blessed One saw the Venerable Sāriputta sitting not far away, cross-legged, holding his body straight, contemplating his own peace. Then the Blessed One, having understood the meaning of this, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:

A bhikkhu with peaceful mind,
Has cut the cord of birth and death.
The wandering in birth and death is ended,
Freed from Māra's bonds.

title: - Just as, bhikkhus, a person throws a yoke with a single hole into the great ocean. There is a blind turtle that surfaces once…
content: - Just as, bhikkhus, a person throws a yoke with a single hole into the great ocean. There is a blind turtle that surfaces once every hundred years. What do you think, bhikkhus, would that blind turtle, surfacing once every hundred years, put its neck into that yoke with a single hole?" - "It might, Venerable Sir, after a very long time." - "I say, bhikkhus, that the blind turtle surfacing once every hundred years would put its neck into that yoke with a single hole more quickly than a fool who has fallen into a plane of misery could regain human birth. Why is that? Because there, bhikkhus, there is no practice of Dhamma, no righteous conduct, no wholesome deeds, no meritorious deeds. There, bhikkhus, they devour one another, and the weak are eaten. Why is that? Because they do not see the Four Noble Truths. What four? The Noble Truth of Suffering ... the Noble Truth of the Path leading to the Cessation of Suffering. Therefore, bhikkhus, an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is suffering.' ... an exertion should be made to understand: 'This is the path leading to the cessation of suffering.'

title: There are these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus. What two? Giving of material goods and giving of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of…
content: There are these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus. What two? Giving of material goods and giving of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of giving. The foremost among these two kinds of giving, bhikkhus, is the giving of the Dhamma. There are these two kinds of offerings, bhikkhus. What two? Offering of material goods and offering of the Dhamma. These are the two kinds of offerings. The foremost among these two kinds of offerings, bhikkhus, is the offering of the Dhamma. There are these two kinds of wealth, bhikkhus. What two? Material wealth and Dhamma wealth. These are the two kinds of wealth. The foremost among these two kinds of wealth, bhikkhus, is Dhamma wealth.

title: Elder Sāriputta (continued): One who sees pleasure as suffering, Sees suffering as a dart, Standing in the middle of both — How can the world…
content:
Elder Sāriputta (continued):

One who sees pleasure as suffering,
Sees suffering as a dart,
Standing in the middle of both —
How can the world hold that one?

Not allowing evil desires,
Laziness, weak energy,
Little learning, no faith —
How can the world hold that one?

Much learning, wise,
Well concentrated in virtue,
Focused on mental stillness —
Stand up, be at the forefront.

One who devotes oneself to proliferation,
Like a beast delighting in proliferation,
Falls away, missing Nibbāna,
The unsurpassed security from bondage.

One who abandons proliferation,
Delights in the non-proliferating path,
Reaches Nibbāna,
The unsurpassed security from bondage.

title: Possessing five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cannot attain and abide in right concentration. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cannot endure forms, cannot endure sounds,…
content: Possessing five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cannot attain and abide in right concentration. What five? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cannot endure forms, cannot endure sounds, cannot endure odors, cannot endure tastes, cannot endure touches. Possessing these five qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu cannot attain and abide in right concentration.

title: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu desires gain,…
content: Possessing seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates. What seven? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu desires gain, desires honor, desires praise, has no moral shame, has no moral dread, has evil desires, and has wrong view. Possessing these seven qualities, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not loved, liked, respected, or emulated by his fellow celibates.

title: Bhikkhus, what is painful practice with slow direct knowledge? Here, a person has a very strong greedy nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of…
content: Bhikkhus, what is painful practice with slow direct knowledge? Here, a person has a very strong greedy nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of greed; a very strong hateful nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of hatred; a very strong deluded nature, always experiencing suffering and distress born of delusion. For that person, these five faculties appear very soft: the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom. Because these five faculties are soft, he attains the immediate concentration for the destruction of the taints slowly. This, bhikkhus, is called painful practice with slow direct knowledge.

title: Standing to one side, the devata Kassapa spoke this verse before the Blessed One: With mind liberated, The bhikkhu practices jhāna, And with the wish,…
content:
Standing to one side, the devata Kassapa spoke this verse before the Blessed One:

With mind liberated,
The bhikkhu practices jhāna,
And with the wish,
Attains the heart's desire.
Having known the world's
Rise and fall,
His mind pure, unattached,
He enjoys the true fruit.

title: Elder Phussa: The seer Paṇḍara, seeing many faithful ones, Self-developed, well-guarded and restrained, Then asked the one named Phussa: 'In the future, what desires will…
content:
Elder Phussa:

The seer Paṇḍara, seeing many faithful ones,
Self-developed, well-guarded and restrained,
Then asked the one named Phussa:

'In the future, what desires will there be?
What aspirations? What conduct?
Please answer our question.'

'Seer Paṇḍara, listen to my words,
Receive them carefully, I will speak of the future.

'Anger and resentment,
Concealment and stubbornness,
Much deceit and envy —
Thus it will be in the future.

'Considering themselves wise,
They have gone to the far shore of the profound Dhamma,
They despise the good Dhamma,
They do not respect one another.

'Many dangers in the world
Will occur in the future.
This well-taught Dhamma,
Fools will defile.

'In the Saṅgha, those of inferior virtue
Often proclaim themselves confident and fearless.
The unlearned, the talkative, will gain a strong position.

'In the Saṅgha, those of beautiful virtue,
When they proclaim what is true, are often weak,
Shy and lacking in ardor.

'Silver, gold, fields, land,
Goats and sheep,
Male and female servants —
Fools, lacking wisdom, will accept all these in the future.

'Fools are easily angered, not calm in virtue,
Arrogant, wandering here and there,
Like beasts fond of fighting.

'They become restless, always wearing blue robes,
Deceitful and stubborn, talkative, speaking falsely,
They imitate and pretend to be like the noble ones of old.

'With oil-slicked hair, restless, eyes painted blue,
Wearing ivory-white robes, they walk on the roads.

'The well-dyed yellow robe, the banner of the Arahants,
Worn by the liberated, is not despised by them.
But they despise the yellow robe, longing to wear white.

'They become greedy for gain, lazy, of little energy,
Hard to live with in the wilderness, delighting in village life.

'Those who fear gain, always fond of wrong livelihood,
They imitate such a one, associating, not restrained.

'Those who do not gain [honor], they do not respect or honor
Those worthy of respect, the wise; they do not associate.

'Despising their own banner, delighting in external colors,
Some wear white robes, the banner of outside sects.

'Not respecting the yellow robe, in that time they are thus.
They await the yellow robe, not of a bhikkhu.

'Overcome by suffering, pierced by the dart of pain,
They await great terror.
[But] this elephant does not think about that.

'When the six-tusked elephant saw the well-dyed Arahant banner,
He uttered verses connected with the goal.

'Whoever wears the robe
With mind not free from defilements,
Not self-controlled, not truthful,
Is not worthy of the robe.

'Whoever casts off defilements,
Well established in virtue,
Self-controlled, truthful,
Is indeed worthy of the robe.

'An immoral person of inferior wisdom,
Not self-controlled, greedy,
With distracted mind, uninspired,
Is not worthy of the robe.

'One complete in virtue,
Free from greed, concentrated,
With truly pure mind,
That one is worthy of the robe.

'Whoever is arrogant and heedless,
Foolish, without virtue,
Deserves to wear white —
What need has that one of a robe?

'Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs with defiled minds, without faith,
Will in the future oppress those with compassionate minds.

'Fools wearing robes, though taught by elders,
Of weak wisdom, will not listen, not self-controlled, greedy.

'Though taught thus, fools will not respect one another,
Will not obey the words of the teacher,
Like a wild horse [fails to obey] the charioteer.

'Thus in the future, conduct will be like that.
Bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, when the final time comes,
Be gentle and friendly, respect one another.

'Before this great calamity comes, before the great calamity arrives,
Be gentle and friendly, respect one another.

'Have a mind of loving-kindness and compassion,
Well restrained in virtue,
Devoted to energy and effort,
Always persistently inspired.

'Seeing the danger in heedlessness,
Security in non-heedlessness,
Develop the Noble Eightfold Path,
Realize the Deathless path.'

title: Whatever causes — if the mind faculty were unrestrained — would give rise to craving, sorrow, and unwholesome states, that he restrains; he guards the…
content: Whatever causes — if the mind faculty were unrestrained — would give rise to craving, sorrow, and unwholesome states, that he restrains; he guards the mind faculty, undertakes the restraint of the mind faculty. By means of this noble restraint of the faculties, he experiences inner well-being, without disturbance.
